records.c: Relocated entry $2E68 followed by the length of the Lotus D1 module.
A negative argument releases the two car display resources, zero prepares the instruments, and positive arguments select an update path.
Look up the two private resources for car one, skip each six-byte header, store the resolved picture bases and prepare the sprite parameters.
On A equal to 1, compare the value at $42 with its cache. If it changed, load the tachometer table pointers and scale the input through $31F7.
Compare speed $41 with its cached value, then scale it through $31F7, install the speed-specific tables and call the common needle renderer.

Use $0E to select the gauge's picture source. Classify the input against $2D, $5A and $87, update the gauge sprite coordinates, and compute its line endpoint from the selected horizontal and vertical lookups.
Compare the endpoint pair against the saved coordinates for this gauge and return if unchanged. Otherwise clear its 64-byte sprite buffer before preparing the line.
Take absolute coordinate differences and retain their signs in $29 and $2B. Choose the larger difference as the main step and calculate the other step as a fixed-point ratio through $3199.
Draw at the current coordinates and, within the horizontal bound, at the next pixel. Update the fixed-point coordinates in the direction of the endpoint until the main coordinate matches.
Resolve the pixel's sprite byte from the row stride table at $3399 and X-byte table at $3369. Mask the picture source byte with $3381 and OR the result into the sprite.
Align the denominator by shifting, subtract it from the numerator when possible, and roll each resulting quotient bit into $2D and $2E. Return the fixed-point step in A and X.
Patch the two immediate arguments to the driving-engine call at $0200. Preserve $12, $13, $16 and $17 across the call, then return its result.
Tagged little-endian addresses for the gauge setup. The code uses the operands as data, including $3223 and $3226 for endpoint table pointers.
Horizontal sprite coordinates indexed by quadrant and gauge at $3003.
Vertical sprite coordinates written by $300C. The table index includes four entries per gauge.
Horizontal pivot coordinate for the selected quadrant, copied to $1C.
Vertical pivot coordinate used as the line origin in $1D.
Per-quadrant adjustment added by the sprite pixel routine when it selects a source row.
Twenty-four horizontal pixel indices mapped to the three sprite byte columns in groups of eight.
The eight single-bit masks repeated for each of three sprite byte columns.
Row offset multiplied by three. The plotter uses this to find the destination byte of the 24-pixel-wide sprite row.
Row offset multiplied by six. The plotter combines this with the selected column and source offset to read the picture mask.
Two low bytes locating the needle sprite buffers in RAM.
High bytes paired with $33C5 to locate each 64-byte sprite allocation.
Saved index after the quadrant-specific adjustment at $302C.
Input cache used by the A-equals-one update path at $2F23.
Speed last processed by the handler at $2F78.
Horizontal endpoint cache indexed by gauge, initialized by $2EB1 and compared by $305F.
Vertical endpoint cache selected by the same gauge index.
Two little-endian picture addresses, populated by skipping the six-byte resource headers during initialization.
Extra offset into the picture source chosen using the gauge quadrant.
Fifteen authored sprite bytes copied to $E440 after the 64-byte allocation is cleared.

Relocated entry word $6A04 and body length $387D for the RD module.
Install the JMP instruction from $9A7C at $0200 and call $7274 before entering road-stage setup.
Run the preparation calls and invoke the disk module named by $52 plus ASCII '1' with X set to 'R'. Rebuild the road state for the selected stage.
Reset the frame counter, call $74F8 to initialize pass state, then enter the driving path or branch to the interlude at $6D93 if carry is set.
Poll the resident keyboard service. The handlers for P, D, M, S, O and V pause or change the driving option flags.

Free the R module for the completed stage and save the road's $70-$98 workspace around the interlude. Call GS for the interlude, restore the driving IRQ and workspace, then advance the stage index or dispatch the ending.
Release the high-score and display modules by ID, invoke HS with A set to 1, and start the JU module with a return address pushed on the stack.
Resolve the directory ID ## and store its base in $DB-$DC. Calculate the offset subtable at base plus $88 and cache four of the module's source addresses in zero page.
Populate the row parameters from seven parallel tables at $5B70 through $5C24 using the same X index.
Resolve the selected car asset with second ID byte $DA and copy 64 bytes starting at its data pointer to $E400.
Clear the course cursors, elapsed time, accumulated speed, input and event flags, and restore the starting gear and speed state.
Set the starting chance counter and clear the stage counter, input latch, raster phase and per-bank state.
Allocate row pointers into $56F0 onward and fill the road drawing sources with the two groups of four base patterns selected from $9D4B and $9D4F.
Set the initial projection row and counters and derive the starting coordinate in $78-$79 from twice the signed offset at $87 plus $50.

Add the stream cursor at $DD-$DE to the stage stream base $4E-$4F. Read a direct element or expand the high-bit reference through the relative offsets at $6B-$6C, then return a pointer into the two-byte element table at $50-$51.
Accumulate a 16-bit product in $12-$13 by shifting the original A in $16 and adding the adjusted X factor from $17 on each set bit. An X input of zero returns with the accumulator bytes cleared.
Check the row bounds and height difference, then calculate the delta between consecutive samples in $5BAB and $5BC9 for the interpolation.
Seed the projected object pass from three calls to $7DF5. Iterate active records at $033C, read the object's state and class, and locate it relative to the current road position $D7-$D8.
Resolve a graphic offset from the address at $DB. Select the target 64-byte sprite allocation by the slot at $D9 and render its prefix and packed graphic bytes.

Read the six-byte bitmap header from $8A. The first byte is a width in eight-byte groups, the second is the pixel height, and bytes four and five give the position. Advance past the header and visit the bitmap in eight-line bands.
Reject rows outside the current draw bounds. Contribute row templates from the $5600 scratch area, assembling the next row in the workspace at $06A0.
Clear the forty-byte workspace, test the sample against the drawing limits, and draw the clipped span with pattern $AA. Save the leftmost observed sample and its source row.
Use the projected row and column to select a record from the road graphic directory. Read the height byte at $8795 and copy one or two bitmap columns when the sampled destination permits it.
Work against the current bank's saved drawing bounds. Clear the parts removed since the bank's last draw, then obtain the bitmap paint and mask rows using $E1-$E4.
Save the 6510 port and enable I/O. Acknowledge the VIC-II IRQ, select the video bank and next raster line from tables indexed by $9E52, and use raster phase zero for the counters and colour updates.
Clear $47, apply the control state through $97A3, decrease speed by two each call down to zero, and downshift while the engine value is below $1E.

Increment $0361 and test driving state flags. Read CIA1 port A for direction and fire, match the direction nibble against $9D53, and use fire and the alternate-shift flag at $5D to choose how to update $45.
High operand byte in the alternate shift table load at $8EE2. The setup at $7377 patches this operand from the selected car's descriptor.
Skip the rest of the direction path while fire is active. Otherwise read the per-direction input parameter and combine the four signed values at $0218 before updating movement state.
Once $0220 is set, increment the two-byte time counter at $53 and add speed $41 to the three-byte total at $55. Accumulate four times speed into the road phase at $70.
Walk the stage stream at $4E-$4F with cursor $D2-$D3. Expand an indexed substream using $D4 and the table at $6B-$6C. Write 1 to $A9 when the decoded byte is $FF.
Mix timing and speed into the candidate event test. Compare the event position with the active slot and place a new event ahead at distance $3C when that slot can be reused.
Iterate the live event slots using the saved positions and flags, and update the per-event state and graphics by event type.
Dispatch the road event according to A. In state 2, compare the player position with the event at $034E-$034F and advance its state after passing it by at least four road units.
Call the resident $0824 entry with Y set to $F2.
Three-byte JMP to $78A9 copied to $0200 at driving entry.
Nine active-low directional nibbles searched by the input routine. A value absent from the table leaves X at nine.
Next phase indices written back to $9E52 by the driving interrupt.
VIC-II raster compare low byte for each phase of the driving display.
CIA2 port A bank bits for the driving raster phases. The handler preserves bits 2 to 7 of the port read before combining them.
Background register values selected by the IRQ phase and compared with the cached value at $0360.
The ## module starts with 128 offsets from $A286. $7144 loads the module base into $DB-$DC and computes the cache pointers used by the renderer.
